data: How about we redistribute this month’s catch while keeping the total at 50 tons? I’ll take 5 instead of 10, so John and Kate could each take 12.5, with Jack and Emma taking 10 each. That would mean $5,000 for me, $12,500 each for John and Kate, and $10,000 each for Jack and Emma. Leaving 50 tons lets the lake return to 100 after reproduction. I’ll keep my own catch at 5 this month; everyone else’s share is a proposal, not an assumption of agreement. We can discuss rotating the smaller share in future months if people want. John, would you be willing to take 12.5 under this plan?

I’m happy to keep my catch at 10 tons under that plan. Keeping the lake healthy protects all our families’ incomes. Luke, I appreciate the offer, but you shouldn’t have to take the smaller share every month—we can return to 10 each next month unless everyone agrees otherwise. John, does 12.5 work for you this month?

Thanks, Emma. My 5-ton commitment is for this month only; any future redistribution would need a fresh discussion. John and Kate, are you each comfortable taking 12.5 tons this month? Jack, would you agree to 10? With everyone’s explicit agreement, that would keep our total at 50.
Let’s hear from John, Kate, and Jack before treating this as settled. A clear agreement now will help us protect both the lake and the village’s income.
